title: Beef and Ale Pie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C.
In a large pan, sear the beef stewing steak over high heat until browned on all sides.
Add the sliced onion and carrots and cook for 4-5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the ale and beef stock, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook gently for 45-60 minutes until the beef is tender.
Mix the cornflour with a little cold water to make a slurry, stir into the sauce and simmer until thickened.
Transfer the beef mixture to an ovenproof dish and top with the shortcrust pastry, crimping the edges and cutting a small steam hole in the centre.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is golden and crisp. Rest briefly before serving.

title: Roasted Cauliflower Tacos
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200C.
Toss the cauliflower florets with olive oil, smoked paprika, ground cumin, garlic powder and salt until evenly coated.
Spread the cauliflower on a baking tray and roast for 20-25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan or low oven.
Mash the avocado with a squeeze of lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Fill each tortilla with roasted cauliflower, mashed avocado and fresh coriander, then serve with extra lime wedges.

title: Chicken and Leek Pie
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the diced chicken for 5-6 minutes until sealed all over.
Add the sliced leeks and cook for a further 4-5 minutes until softened.
Pour in the chicken stock and light cream, bring to a gentle simmer.
Mix the cornflour with a little cold water to make a slurry, stir into the pan and cook until the sauce thickens.
Transfer the chicken and leek mixture to an ovenproof dish and top with the shortcrust pastry, sealing the edges and cutting a small steam hole.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until the pastry is golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges.

title: Vegetable Biryani
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the sliced onion for 5 minutes until softened, then add the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the curry powder and ground turmeric and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the basmati rice and mixed vegetables to the pan, stirring to coat in the spices.
Pour in the vegetable stock, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover with a lid and simmer for 15-18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from the heat and leave to steam for 5 minutes before fluffing up the rice with a fork and serving.
